title: Lab: Stand Up Prometheus + Grafana
intro_md: Bring up a monitoring stack with Docker Compose, verify scraping, query with PromQL, and check alert state — the loop you'll run whenever you adopt a new service.

steps.instruction_md: Start the monitoring stack defined in the current directory's compose file, detached.
steps.mock_output:
[+] Running 3/3
 ✔ Container prometheus     Started
 ✔ Container node-exporter  Started
 ✔ Container grafana        Started

steps.instruction_md: Verify Prometheus itself is up by querying its health endpoint with curl (http://localhost:9090/-/healthy).
Check node_exporter is exposing metrics: fetch its endpoint and show only lines starting with `node_load` (pipe to grep).
steps.hint: Exporters serve plaintext at /metrics on their own port (node_exporter: 9100).

steps.instruction_md: Query the Prometheus HTTP API for the `up` metric (endpoint /api/v1/query, parameter query=up).
steps.hint: GET /api/v1/query?query=up — quote the URL so the shell keeps the ? intact.

steps.instruction_md: Simulate an outage: stop the node-exporter container.
Ask Prometheus which targets are down: query `up == 0` via the API (URL-encode the spaces as %20 or quote the URL).
steps.hint: The same query endpoint accepts any PromQL expression — `up == 0` finds dead targets.
